mainTopic: The בכור's double portion only from the father, and the source that a husband inherits his wife
overview: This amud begins at the end of a story: רבי ינאי walks away from a questioner who, he says, does not really want to learn. The גמרא then asks for the source that a בכור does not take a double portion of his mother's estate. אביי learns it from ״לוֹ״ ('to him, not to her'). רב נחמן בר יצחק learns it from ״אוֹנוֹ״ ('his strength, not hers'), and the extra ו in that word is shown to teach two lessons. But each of these proofs might cover only a narrow case. So רבא gives the final source, ״לוֹ מִשְׁפַּט הַבְּכֹרָה״: the firstborn's right exists only for a man. Next the גמרא turns to the משנה's rule that a husband inherits his wife and she does not inherit him. A ברייתא reads ״שְׁאֵרוֹ״ as his wife, and אביי and רבא argue over how the פסוק must be read to fit that. רבי עקיבא learns the rule from ״וְיָרַשׁ אוֹתָהּ״. רבי ישמעאל instead proves it from the פסוקים about land moving between tribes, from the hill of פנחס, and from the cities of יאיר. The point of the יאיר proof comes on the next amud.

steps.title: The sage asks to be taken away from a questioner who does not want to learn
steps.stepSummary: The sage (רבי ינאי) tells his attendant to lead him away, because the questioner is not really trying to learn.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to his attendant: "Take me away. This man does not want to learn."
steps.whatsHappening: This is the end of a story from the previous lines. The sage was asked about a בכור in his mother's estate, and he ends the conversation in frustration.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The sage felt the questions were easy to answer and were being asked to push back, not to understand. Walking away shows he thought the rule was clear. That is why the גמרא now goes looking for the clear source.

keyTerms.meaning: His attendant, the student who served and helped him
Lead me away, take me from here

phrases.english: He said to his attendant: Take me away,
this one does not want to learn.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the story that began before this section.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The sage holds that the rule (no double portion for a בכור in his mother's estate) is clear and that the objections were not real questions.

steps.title: What is the reason for the rule?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the source that a בכור does not get a double portion in his mother's estate.
steps.simpleTranslation: And what is the reason?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא sets up the next move. It asks where the rule comes from, so that an answer can follow.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The story told us the rule but not its source. The גמרא wants a פסוק that shows the double portion is only in the father's estate.

phrases.english: And what is the reason?
phrases.notes: He means: why does a בכור not get a double share of what his mother leaves?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the source behind the rule the sage treated as obvious.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The פסוק that limits the בכור's double portion to the father's estate.

steps.title: אביי: the word ״לוֹ״ means him, not her
steps.stepSummary: אביי reads ״בְּכֹל אֲשֶׁר יִמָּצֵא לוֹ״ as limiting the double portion to what the father owns.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: The פסוק says "of all that is found to him." "To him" teaches that it is not "to her."
steps.whatsHappening: אביי answers the question with a word in the פסוק. The double portion is "in all that is found to him," meaning the father, not the mother.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אביי focuses on the masculine word ״לוֹ״, 'to him.' He reads it as leaving out what is found 'to her,' the mother's estate. So the double portion applies only to the father's property.

keyTerms.meaning: The פסוק says (introduces a source in the תורה)
Is found to him, meaning what he owns

phrases.english: Abaye said: The verse says:
"Of all that is found to him";
phrases.notes: דברים 21:17

phrases.english: "to him" – and not to her.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 2.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The word ״לוֹ״ limits the double portion to the father's estate.

steps.title: Maybe ״לוֹ״ only covers a man who married a widow
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests ״לוֹ״ may only exclude a case where the son is the father's firstborn but not the mother's. If both parents were first-timers, maybe he does take double from her.
steps.simpleTranslation: But say this only applies to a בחור who married an אלמנה. But a בחור who married a בתולה, in that case too he should take a double portion from her!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on אביי's proof. It says the word ״לוֹ״ may only work for a narrower case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When a בחור marries an אלמנה who already has children, the son is the father's first but not the mother's first. So ״לוֹ״ might only mean he gets double from his father, since only to him is he a בכור. But when a בחור marries a בתולה, the son is the first for both of them, and ״לוֹ״ may not stop him from taking double from his mother too.

keyTerms.meaning: These words apply (only to this case)
An unmarried young man, marrying for the first time
A widow (here, one who already has children)
A woman marrying for the first time

steps.confusionAlert: The challenge does not argue that a בכור always takes double from his mother. It only says ״לוֹ״ may be too narrow to prove the rule for every case.

phrases.english: But say: this applies only to
a bachelor who married a widow,
but a bachelor who married a virgin –
so too, he should take [a double portion from her]!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאֵימָא: הָנֵי מִילֵּי בָּחוּר שֶׁנָּשָׂא אַלְמָנָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges אביי's proof as too narrow.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: ״לוֹ״ may only exclude a son who is firstborn to the father alone. It may not exclude a son who is firstborn to both parents.

steps.title: רב נחמן בר יצחק: ״אוֹנוֹ״ means his strength, not hers
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן בר יצחק brings a different word from the same פסוק, ״רֵאשִׁית אֹנוֹ״, to tie the בכור's rights to the father only.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן בר יצחק said: The פסוק says "the first of his strength." "His strength" teaches that it is not "her strength."
steps.whatsHappening: A new source is brought to answer the challenge. The double portion depends on being the first of the father's strength, not the mother's.
steps.deeperAnalysis: ״אוֹנוֹ״ ties the בכור's status to the father's strength, not the mother's. רב נחמן בר יצחק means this to rule out a double portion from the mother in every case, including the בחור who married a בתולה. Step 8 will challenge whether it really reaches that far.

keyTerms.meaning: The first of his strength (a name for the firstborn)

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן בַּר יִצְחָק, אָמַר קְרָא:
phrases.english: Rav Naḥman bar Yitzḥak said: The verse says:
"The first of his strength";
phrases.notes: דברים 21:17

phrases.english: "his strength" – and not her strength.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן בַּר יִצְחָק, אָמַר קְרָא: ״רֵאשִׁית אֹנוֹ״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 4 with a new source.
steps.terutzResolutionType: New derivation from a different word in the same פסוק
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Only ״לוֹ״ was available, which might cover only the widow case.
steps.terutzMaskana: ״אוֹנוֹ״ ties firstborn rights to the father in every case, so the mother's estate is never split with a double portion.

steps.title: ״אוֹנוֹ״ is already needed for a son born after נפלים
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects that ״אוֹנוֹ״ is used for a different teaching: a son born after נפלים is still a בכור for inheritance.
steps.simpleTranslation: But that word is needed for a son who came after נפלים, to teach that he is a בכור for נחלה. The firstborn is one whose father's heart is pained over him, which leaves out a baby whose father's heart is not pained over him!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רב נחמן בר יצחק. It says the word ״אוֹנוֹ״ is already used up for another teaching, so it cannot also teach "not her strength."
steps.deeperAnalysis: ״אוֹנוֹ״ is read as tied to grief: the father grieves over a son who lived. A נפל (a baby that was not viable) does not cause that grief, so it does not count as the first. The next son born alive is the בכור for inheritance. If the word teaches that, it seems it cannot also exclude the mother's estate.

keyTerms.meaning: Babies born not able to live
His heart is pained over him (he grieves for him)

steps.confusionAlert: This son is a בכור for inheritance even though he may not be a בכור for other laws. Being a בכור can depend on which law we are talking about.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows a common pattern in the גמרא: a word in a פסוק that is already used for one teaching usually cannot be used for a second one.

phrases.english: That [word] is needed
for one who came after non-viable babies,
that he should be a firstborn for inheritance –
[the firstborn is] one whose heart is pained over him,
phrases.notes: ״אוֹנוֹ״ sounds like the word for grief, so it is read as "the one he grieves over." The heart here is the father's.

phrases.aramaic: יָצָא זֶה שֶׁאֵין לִבּוֹ דָּוֶוה עָלָיו!
phrases.english: excluding this one whose heart is not pained over him!

steps.triggerLanguage: הָהוּא מִבַּעְיָא לֵיהּ לַבָּא אַחַר נְפָלִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the derivation of step 5 by showing the word is already used.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב נחמן בר יצחק's use of ״אוֹנוֹ״ in step 5.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: ״אוֹנוֹ״ already teaches that a son born after נפלים is a בכור for inheritance, so it is not free to teach "not her strength."

steps.title: The extra letter in 'his strength' teaches two things
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers the objection from step 6. If the פסוק only wanted to teach about a son born after נפלים, it could have said ״אוֹן״. The extra ו in ״אוֹנוֹ״ (his strength) teaches a second lesson: the בכור's rights come from the father.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, the verse should have said 'for he is the first of strength.' Why does it say 'his strength'? Learn two things from it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the last objection. It shows that ״אוֹנוֹ״ can teach both lessons at once.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The objection said ״אוֹנוֹ״ was already used for the נפלים teaching. The answer is that the plain word ״אוֹן״ would have been enough for that. The extra 'his' is free to teach that a בכור's rights are tied to the father's strength, not the mother's.

keyTerms.meaning: His strength; the ו at the end means 'his'
Let the verse say; the פסוק could have used shorter wording

phrases.english: If so, let the verse say:
"For he is the first of strength"
phrases.notes: Notice the missing 'his.' This is the shorter wording the פסוק could have used.

phrases.english: Why does it say "his strength"?
Learn two things from it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the objection in step 6 that ״אוֹנוֹ״ is already used for another teaching.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Extra wording: the extra letter teaches a second lesson.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: ״אוֹנוֹ״ is fully used up by the נפלים teaching, so it cannot teach about the mother.
steps.terutzMaskana: ״אוֹן״ alone would teach the נפלים lesson. The extra ו teaches that בכורה rights come only from the father.

steps.title: Maybe this only excludes a widower's second wife
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the proof from ״אוֹנוֹ״. Maybe it only excludes a widower who married a virgin. There, the son is not the father's first strength. But if a bachelor married a virgin, the son is first to both parents, so maybe he does take double from his mother.
steps.simpleTranslation: But still, say this applies to a widower who married a virgin. But a bachelor who married a virgin, so too the son would take a double share.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks רב נחמן בר יצחק's proof from ״אוֹנוֹ״ again. This time it argues the proof does not cover every case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: ״אוֹנוֹ״ excludes a son who is not the father's first. That happens with a widower who already had children. But when a bachelor marries a virgin, the son is the father's first strength and the mother's first child. So ״אוֹנוֹ״ does not tell us he loses a double share from his mother.

keyTerms.meaning: A virgin bride, never had children

phrases.english: But still, say these words apply only
to a widower who married a virgin,
but a bachelor who married a virgin,
so too the son would take a double share!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After step 7 defends ״אוֹנוֹ״, this step shows it still leaves a gap, like the gap in step 4.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב נחמן בר יצחק's proof from ״רֵאשִׁית אֹנוֹ״
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: ״אוֹנוֹ״ only excludes a son who isn't the father's first. It says nothing about a son who is first to both parents.

steps.title: רבא: the firstborn's right belongs to a man
steps.stepSummary: רבא brings a new source, ״לוֹ מִשְׁפַּט הַבְּכֹרָה״. The right of the בכור exists only for a man, never for a woman. This covers every case, including a bachelor who married a virgin.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רבא said: The verse says, 'The right of the firstborn is his.' The firstborn's right is for a man, and not for a woman.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא drops the earlier proofs and gives a new source that closes the gap.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The earlier proofs (״לוֹ״ from ״בְּכֹל אֲשֶׁר יִמָּצֵא לוֹ״ and ״אוֹנוֹ״) only tied the son to his father, which left the bachelor case open. רבא reads ״לוֹ״ as saying the whole law of בכורה belongs to men. So a mother's estate never gives a double share, in any case.

keyTerms.meaning: The law or right of the firstborn: the double portion
To him; here read as 'to a man only'

steps.confusionAlert: Both אביי and רבא use the word ״לוֹ״, but from different places. אביי used it from ״בְּכֹל אֲשֶׁר יִמָּצֵא לוֹ״. רבא uses it from ״לוֹ מִשְׁפַּט הַבְּכֹרָה״.
steps.whatToRemember: The final source that a בכור gets no double portion from his mother is רבא's: ״לוֹ מִשְׁפַּט הַבְּכֹרָה״. The right of the firstborn belongs to a man, not a woman.

phrases.english: Rather, Rava said: The verse says:
"The right of the firstborn is his"
phrases.notes: דברים 21:17

phrases.english: the firstborn's right is for a man,
and the firstborn's right is not for a woman.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the proofs that step 8 weakened with a new source that covers every case.
steps.terutzResolutionType: New source from the same פסוק
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A son who is first to both parents might take a double share from his mother.
steps.terutzMaskana: The law of בכורה exists only for men, so a mother's estate never gives a double share.

steps.title: What is the source that a husband inherits his wife?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא moves to the next line of the משנה, 'a man inherits his wife.' It asks for the source of this rule.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'And a man with his wife, etc.' From where do we know these words?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new topic. It quotes the next part of the משנה and asks for its source, setting up the ברייתא that follows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה taught that a husband inherits his wife but she does not inherit him. The גמרא wants a פסוק for both halves of that rule.

keyTerms.meaning: From where do we know these words? A request for a source
Etc.; the rest of the משנה's line

phrases.english: "And a man with his wife, etc."
phrases.notes: Quoting the משנה: a man inherits his wife, but she doesn't inherit him.

phrases.english: From where do we know these words?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָאִישׁ אֶת אִשְׁתּוֹ וְכוּ׳. מְנָהָנֵי מִילֵּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Ends the בכור discussion and opens the next line of the משנה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The source in the תורה that a husband inherits his wife and she does not inherit him.

steps.title: ''His kin'' is his wife, and ''he inherits her'' only
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא reads ״שְׁאֵרוֹ״ (his kin) as his wife, which teaches that a husband inherits her. It then asks whether she inherits him too. It answers no, from ״וְיָרַשׁ אוֹתָהּ״: he inherits her, and she does not inherit him.
steps.simpleTranslation: As the Rabbis taught: 'His kin' means his wife. This teaches that a husband inherits his wife. Might she also inherit him? The verse teaches: 'and he shall inherit her.' He inherits her, and she does not inherit him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers with a ברייתא that gives a source for both halves of the משנה's rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word ״שְׁאֵרוֹ״ in the inheritance פסוק is read as 'his wife,' so the husband inherits. The ending ״אוֹתָהּ״ is feminine, which shows the inheriting goes one way only: from wife to husband. That blocks the idea that she also inherits him.

keyTerms.meaning: The Rabbis taught; introduces a ברייתא
His kin; read here as his wife
One might think; introduces an idea the ברייתא will reject
The verse teaches; brings the proof that settles the question

steps.whatToRemember: A husband inherits his wife, from ״שְׁאֵרוֹ״. She does not inherit him, from ״וְיָרַשׁ אוֹתָהּ״.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the תורה source for the rule that inheritance between husband and wife goes only one way.

phrases.english: As the Rabbis taught:
"His kin": this is his wife,
phrases.notes: במדבר 27:11

phrases.english: which teaches that a husband inherits his wife.
One might think she also inherits him?
The verse teaches: "And he shall inherit her"
phrases.notes: Literally 'it,' but the word is feminine, so it can also be read as 'her.'

phrases.english: he inherits her,
and she does not inherit him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 10's request for a source.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: ״שְׁאֵרוֹ״ means his wife, so the husband inherits her. ״וְיָרַשׁ אוֹתָהּ״ limits inheritance to one direction: he inherits her, not she him.

steps.title: The verse doesn't read that way
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects that the order of the words in the פסוק does not support the ברייתא's reading.
steps.simpleTranslation: But the verses are not written like this!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the ברייתא from step 11. In the actual פסוק, the inheritance is given 'to his kin,' so if 'kin' means the wife, the wife would be inheriting the husband.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא wanted ״שְׁאֵרוֹ״ to be the one being inherited from. But in the פסוק's word order, ״שְׁאֵרוֹ״ is the one who receives. So the reading seems to teach the opposite of what the ברייתא said.

phrases.english: But the verses are not written like this!
phrases.notes: The פסוק (במדבר 27:11) says to give the inheritance 'to his kin,' which sounds like the wife inherits the husband, the opposite.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the ברייתא's reading of ״שְׁאֵרוֹ״ given in step 11.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא's claim that ״שְׁאֵרוֹ״ (his wife) teaches that a husband inherits his wife.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: In the פסוק the inheritance goes TO ״שְׁאֵרוֹ״. If ״שְׁאֵרוֹ״ is the wife, then she inherits him, not the other way around.

steps.title: אביי splits the verse into two parts
steps.stepSummary: אביי rereads the פסוק as two separate phrases, so that the husband inherits ״שְׁאֵרוֹ״, his wife.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: Answer like this: 'Then you shall give his inheritance to the one close to him.' Then, separately: 'His kin, he shall inherit her.'
steps.whatsHappening: אביי answers the problem by dividing the פסוק into two. The first part is a general rule about relatives. The second part says the husband inherits his kin, his wife.
steps.deeperAnalysis: By separating ״שְׁאֵרוֹ״ from the first half of the פסוק, ״שְׁאֵרוֹ״ no longer receives the inheritance. Now it goes with ״וְיָרַשׁ אֹתָהּ״, meaning he inherits her. To do this, אביי also has to drop the ל from ״לִשְׁאֵרוֹ״.

keyTerms.meaning: answer it like this / arrange it like this
the one who is close to him

phrases.english: Abaye said: Answer it like this:
"Then you shall give his inheritance
to the one who is close to him,"
phrases.notes: This first half is a general rule about relatives. אביי stops the פסוק here.

phrases.english: "His kin, and he shall inherit her."
phrases.notes: Notice the ל of ״לִשְׁאֵרוֹ״ is gone, so now the husband inherits his kin.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the objection of step 12.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rearranging the פסוק: splitting it into two phrases.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The פסוק reads straight through, so the inheritance is given to ״שְׁאֵרוֹ״.
steps.terutzMaskana: Read ״שְׁאֵרוֹ וְיָרַשׁ אֹתָהּ״ as its own phrase: the husband inherits his wife.

steps.title: רבא rejects cutting up the verse
steps.stepSummary: רבא objects that you cannot slice a פסוק apart as if with a knife.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: Does a sharp knife cut up verses?!
steps.whatsHappening: רבא pushes back on אביי's answer. Chopping the פסוק into pieces and rearranging it is too drastic.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אביי moved phrases around and dropped a letter. רבא's complaint is about breaking up the פסוק's order. He is not disputing the law that a husband inherits his wife.

phrases.english: Rava said:
Does a sharp knife cut up verses?!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects אביי's method from step 13.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Only אביי's way of reading the פסוק, not the law itself.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: It breaks up the פסוק and rearranges its parts, which is too forced.

steps.title: רבא moves two letters to make 'to him'
steps.stepSummary: רבא reads the פסוק as 'give the inheritance of his kin to him.' He takes letters from two words to form ״לוֹ״, based on the rule גורעין ומוסיפין ודורשין.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רבא said, this is what it is saying: 'And you shall give the inheritance of his kin to him.' He holds that we may subtract letters and add them elsewhere, and then expound.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא gives his own answer to the problem from step 12. He keeps the פסוק in order but shifts two letters.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He takes the ו off ״נַחֲלָתוֹ״ and the ל off ״לִשְׁאֵרוֹ״ and puts them together to make ״לוֹ״, 'to him.' Now the פסוק says the inheritance of his kin (his wife) goes to him (the husband). This works only because רבא holds the rule of גורעין ומוסיפין ודורשין.

keyTerms.meaning: we subtract letters, add them elsewhere, and then expound
the inheritance of his kin (his wife)

steps.whatToRemember: Everyone here agrees that a husband inherits his wife. אביי reaches it by splitting the פסוק, and רבא by moving two letters to make ״לוֹ״.
steps.confusionAlert: רבא is not adding new letters to the תורה. He moves letters that are already there: the ו from ״נַחֲלָתוֹ״ and the ל from ״לִשְׁאֵרוֹ״.

phrases.english: Rather, Rava said, this is what it is saying:
"And you shall give the inheritance of his kin to him"
phrases.notes: The ו from ״נַחֲלָתוֹ״ and the ל from ״לִשְׁאֵרוֹ״ join together to make ״לוֹ״, 'to him.'

phrases.english: He holds that we subtract and add, and then expound.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces אביי's rejected answer with a new way to answer step 12.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Moving letters between words (גורעין ומוסיפין ודורשין).
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The inheritance goes to ״שְׁאֵרוֹ״, so the wife would inherit.
steps.terutzMaskana: The inheritance of ״שְׁאֵרוֹ״ goes ״לוֹ״, to the husband.

steps.title: רבי עקיבא learns it from 'he shall inherit her'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings another ברייתא. In it, רבי עקיבא learns that a husband inherits his wife from ״וְיָרַשׁ אוֹתָהּ״.
steps.simpleTranslation: And this תנא brings it from here. As it is taught: 'And he shall inherit her' teaches that the husband inherits his wife. These are the words of רבי עקיבא.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows that another ברייתא uses a different source for the same law. רבי עקיבא learns it from the words ״וְיָרַשׁ אוֹתָהּ״.
steps.deeperAnalysis: ״אוֹתָהּ״ is a feminine word, so it can mean 'her.' 'He shall inherit her' then means the husband inherits his wife. This needs none of the rearranging that אביי and רבא used.

keyTerms.meaning: a sage of the משנה period
as it is taught in a ברייתא

phrases.english: And this tanna brings it from here –
as it is taught: "And he shall inherit her,"
phrases.notes: ״אוֹתָהּ״ is feminine, so it is read as 'her,' meaning the wife.

phrases.english: this teaches that the husband inherits his wife;
these are the words of Rabbi Akiva.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the אביי and רבא discussion and brings a different ברייתא with another source for the same law.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי עקיבא: ״וְיָרַשׁ אוֹתָהּ״ teaches that a husband inherits his wife.

steps.title: רבי ישמעאל: the tribal-land verse already assumes it
steps.stepSummary: רבי ישמעאל says no special source is needed. The פסוק about an heiress marrying within her tribe already assumes that her husband inherits her.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי ישמעאל says: It is not needed. For the פסוק says, 'And every daughter who inherits a portion from the tribes of the children of Israel shall be a wife to one of the family' and so on. The פסוק is talking about land passing to another tribe through the husband.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי ישמעאל disagrees that we need a special source. He shows that another פסוק already takes it for granted that a husband inherits his wife.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תורה told a daughter who inherited land to marry within her tribe, so the land would not move to another tribe. The land could only move to another tribe if her husband inherits her when she dies. So that פסוק already assumes the husband inherits his wife.

keyTerms.meaning: transfer (of the land) through the husband

steps.whatToRemember: All the opinions agree that a husband inherits his wife. They only argue about which פסוק teaches it: ״שְׁאֵרוֹ״ (the first ברייתא, which אביי and רבא each explain), ״וְיָרַשׁ אוֹתָהּ״ (רבי עקיבא), or the tribal-land פסוק (רבי ישמעאל).
steps.whyThisMatters: רבי ישמעאל's proof shows that the husband's inheritance is so basic that the תורה builds another law on top of it.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yishmael says: It is not needed,
for the verse says:
"And every daughter who inherits a portion
from the tribes of the children of Israel,
[shall be a wife] to one of the family, etc." –
phrases.notes: במדבר 36:8

phrases.english: the verse is speaking about a transfer through the husband.
phrases.notes: Her land would only pass to another tribe if her husband inherits her. So the פסוק takes that for granted.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with רבי עקיבא's need for a special source and offers a different proof.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A husband inherits his wife. This is assumed by the פסוק requiring an heiress to marry within her tribe.

steps.title: Two more verses about land not moving between tribes
steps.stepSummary: רבי ישמעאל adds two more פסוקים from במדבר 36 that warn that an inheritance must not move from one tribe to another.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the פסוק says: 'So shall no inheritance of the children of Israel transfer from tribe to tribe.' And it also says: 'So shall no inheritance transfer from one tribe to another tribe.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי ישמעאל continues his proof by quoting two more פסוקים that warn against land passing from one tribe to another.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Land could only move to another tribe through marriage if a husband inherits his wife. If husbands did not inherit, there would be nothing to worry about. So these warnings also assume that the husband inherits.

keyTerms.meaning: And it says: introduces another פסוק that supports the same point
Will turn or transfer (from one owner to another)

phrases.english: And it says: 'So shall no inheritance transfer
phrases.notes: במדבר 36:7

phrases.english: of the children of Israel from tribe to tribe.'
And it says: 'So shall no inheritance transfer
phrases.notes: במדבר 36:9

phrases.english: from one tribe to another tribe.'

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאוֹמֵר: ״וְלֹא תִסֹּב נַחֲלָה לִבְנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל מִמַּטֶּה אֶל מַטֶּה״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds more פסוקים from the same section of the תורה to support רבי ישמעאל's claim in Step 17.
steps.raayaObject: That a husband inherits his wife, so that land can pass to his tribe.

steps.title: Proof from the hill of פנחס
steps.stepSummary: אלעזר was buried on a hill that belonged to his son פנחס. Since פנחס could not have gotten it from his father, he must have inherited it from his wife.
steps.simpleTranslation: And it says: 'And אלעזר son of אהרן died, and they buried him in the hill of פנחס his son.' Now where did פנחס get land that his father אלעזר did not have? Rather, this teaches that פנחס married a woman, she died, and he inherited her.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי ישמעאל brings a proof from ספר יהושע, from the hill that belonged to פנחס.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A son normally gets land from his father, but here the son owns land that the father does not. The only good explanation is that the land came from פנחס's wife after she died. This shows that a husband inherits his wife.

keyTerms.meaning: The hill of פנחס, land that belonged to him

phrases.english: And it says: 'And Elazar son of Aharon died,
phrases.notes: יהושע 24:33

phrases.english: and they buried him in the hill of Pinchas his son.'
Now from where did Pinchas have land
that Elazar did not have?
Rather, it teaches that Pinchas married a woman
and she died, and he inherited her.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאוֹמֵר: ״וְאֶלְעָזָר בֶּן אַהֲרֹן מֵת, וַיִּקְבְּרוּ אֹתוֹ בְּגִבְעַת פִּנְחָס בְּנוֹ״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the תורה to the נביאים for another proof of the same point.
steps.raayaObject: That a husband inherits his wife.
steps.raayaSupportSource: יהושע 24:33: פנחס owned a hill that his father did not own.

steps.title: Starting the proof from יאיר's cities
steps.stepSummary: רבי ישמעאל quotes a פסוק saying that יאיר son of שגוב had twenty-three cities in the land of גלעד. The question on this פסוק comes next.
steps.simpleTranslation: And it says: 'And שגוב fathered יאיר, who had twenty-three cities in the land of גלעד.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי ישמעאל quotes a third proof, this time from the כתובים. Here he is only setting it up; his point about the פסוק comes right after this.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Like the proof from פנחס, this פסוק will be used to show that a son owned land that seems not to have come from his father. The explanation will again be that it came through a wife.

keyTerms.meaning: The land of גלעד, east of the ירדן

phrases.english: And it says: 'And Seguv fathered Yair,
phrases.notes: דברי הימים א 2:22

phrases.english: and he had twenty-three cities
in the land of Gilead.'

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאוֹמֵר: ״וּשְׂגוּב הוֹלִיד אֶת יָאִיר, וַיְהִי לוֹ עֶשְׂרִים וְשָׁלֹשׁ עָרִים בְּאֶרֶץ הַגִּלְעָד״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the נביאים to the כתובים and begins a proof built the same way as the proof from פנחס.
steps.raayaObject: That a husband inherits his wife (the proof is finished in the next section).
